name: The Inner Loop
description: The Inner Loop is a long-running online forum for people who care about programming as a craft. It started in 2019 as a place for a handful of competitive programmers to share contest problems, and has since drifted into something broader: algorithms, performance engineering, type systems, distributed systems war stories, language design arguments, the occasional code-golf battle. The forum has sections for Problems (puzzles and contest problems), Performance (benchmarks and optimisation arguments), Wat (surprising language behaviour, footguns, near-misses), Design (architecture and API debates), Papers (a half-active reading group), Help (sincere questions from people stuck on something), and Off-Topic. The forum has a bot, `pybot`, that executes any code inside <python>...</python> tags and returns stdout in the same thread — members use it constantly to settle arguments, demo behaviour, or check claims before posting them. There is no moderator hierarchy beyond the original admins, who mostly just keep spam out. The forum has roughly 200 lurkers and maybe fifteen people who actually post. The tone is direct, sometimes blunt, and occasionally warm. People will absolutely tell you you're wrong, but they'll also paste a working snippet to show you why. It's 2026.
default_invitation: A new thread has just opened on the forum. The conversation is active and members are posting throughout the day.
